ReturnPreview.description:
A return preview resource for calculating refund amounts before creating an actual return.
Supports both request (input) and response (output) scenarios using readOnly/writeOnly annotations.

Request fields: items (required), status, restockTriggerStatus, context, orderLevelAdjustmentsRefund, shippingRefund
Response fields: All request fields plus orderId, calculated adjustments, and preview metadata

adjustments.description:
Calculated order-level and shipping adjustments (only present in response).
Includes proportional share of order discounts, fees, additional taxes, and shipping costs
based on the refund modes specified in the request.

allOf.description: Base schema for return preview adjustments

referenceId.description: The ID of the fee, discount, tax, etc. that the adjustment is associated with

name.description: The name of the adjustment (e.g., "Shipping", "Order Discount")

channelId.description: ID of the channel where the return was made

adjustments.description:
Calculated refund adjustments for this item (purchase, taxes, discounts, fees).
Only present in response - calculated by the server based on order data and refund mode.

allOf.description: Base schema for return preview adjustments

referenceId.description: The ID of the fee, discount, tax, etc. that the adjustment is associated with

name.description: The name of the adjustment (e.g., "Sales Tax", "Discount Code"). Not present for PURCHASE type adjustments.

lineItemId.description: The line item id that the return item is associated with

locationId.description: The location ID where the item should be returned

otherReason.description: The reason for the return if the reason is `OTHER`

quantity.description: The quantity of the line item being returned (can be float, e.g., 2.3 Kgs)

restockQuantity.description: The quantity of the line item that will be restocked (can be any number, including 0)

orderId.description: The order ID that the return is associated with (echoed from URL path parameter in response)

orderLevelAdjustmentsRefund.description:
How to handle order-level adjustments refund (discounts, fees, additional taxes).
Only used in request to control calculation mode - not returned in response.

- PRORATED: Distribute refund based on item value proportion
- FULL: Refund all order-level adjustments on first return
- NONE: Do not refund order-level adjustments

preview.description:
Additional preview information with refund totals breakdown (only present in response).
Not included when creating an actual return - this is metadata specific to the preview calculation.

restockTriggerStatus.description: The order return status that triggers automatic inventory adjustment

shippingRefund.description:
How to handle shipping costs refund.
Only used in request to control calculation mode - not returned in response.

- PRORATED: Distribute refund based on item value proportion
- FULL: Refund all shipping costs on first return
- NONE: Do not refund shipping costs

status.description: Order return status (defaults to REQUESTED if not provided)

ReturnPreview.title: ReturnPreview

ReturnPreviewTotal.description:
Breakdown of refund totals by type for return preview calculations.
This schema is specific to the preview endpoint and uses integer representation for calculation simplicity.
All values represent absolute amounts (positive integers) in the smallest currency unit (e.g., cents).

currencyCode.description: Currency code for all amounts (e.g., USD, EUR)

discount.description: Total discount refund amount (includes item and order-level discounts)

fee.description: Total fee refund amount (includes item and order-level fees)

purchase.description: Total purchase refund amount (sum of all item purchase adjustments)

tax.description: Total tax refund amount (includes item taxes, order-level taxes, and shipping taxes)

total.description:
Total refund amount calculated as: purchase + tax + fee + shipping - discount.
All values represent absolute amounts (positive integers).

address.description: An internationalized postal address. Maps to [AddressValidationMetadata](https://github.com/googlei18n/libaddressinput/wiki/AddressValidationMetadata) from Google's Address Data Service and HTML 5.1 [Autofilling form controls: the autocomplete attribute](https://www.w3.org/TR/html51/sec-forms.html#autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute).

addressDetails.description: The non-portable additional address details that are sometimes needed for compliance, risk, or other scenarios where fine-grain address information might be needed. Not portable with common third-party and open-source address libraries and redundant with core fields. For example, `address.addressLine1` is usually a combination of `addressDetails.streetNumber` and `streetName` and `streetType`.

addressType.description: The type of address. Single character representation of a type. For example: 'B' for building, 'F' for organization, 'G' for general delivery, 'H' for high-rise, 'L' for large-volume organization, 'P' for Post Office box or delivery service, 'R' for rural route, 'S' for street, 'U' for unidentified address.

buildingName.description: A named locations that represents the premise. Usually a building name or number or collection of buildings with a common name or number. For example, Craven House.

deliveryService.description: The delivery service. Post office box, bag number, or post office name.

streetName.description: The street name. Just `Drury` in `Drury Lane`.

streetType.description: The street type. For example, avenue, boulevard, road, or expressway.

subBuilding.description: The first-order entity below a named building or location that represents the sub-premise. Usually a single building within a collection of buildings with a common name. Can be a flat, story, floor, room, or apartment.

addressDetails.title: Address Details

addressLine1.description: The first line of the address. For example, number and street name. For example, `3032 Bunker Hill Lane`. Required for compliance and risk checks. Must contain the full address.

addressLine2.description: The second line of the address. For example, office suite or apartment number.

addressLine3.description: The third line of the address, if needed. For example, a street complement for Brazil; direction text, such as `next to Opera House`; or a landmark reference in an Indian address.

adminArea1.description: The highest level sub-division in a country, which is usually a province, state, or ISO-3166-2 subdivision; formatted for postal delivery. For example, `CA` and not `California`. For example, for UK - A county; for USs - A state; for Canada - A province; for Japan - A prefecture; for Switzerland - A kanton.

adminArea2.description: A city, town, or village. Smaller than `adminArea1`.

adminArea3.description: A sub-locality, suburb, neighborhood, or district. Smaller than `adminArea2`. For example, in Brazil - Suburb, bairro, or neighborhood; in India - Sub-locality or district. Street name information may not always available and a sub-locality or district can reference a very small area.

adminArea4.description: The neighborhood, ward, or district. Smaller than `adminArea3` or `subLocality`. For example, the postal sorting code that is used in Guernsey and many French territories, such as French Guiana; the fine-grained administrative levels in China.

postalCode.description: The postal code, which is the zip code or equivalent. Typically required for countries that have a postal code or an equivalent. See [Postal code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postal_code).

address.title: Postal Address (Medium-Grained)

country-code.description: A two-character ISO 3166-1 code that identifies the country or region.

date-time.description: A date and time, in [Internet date and time format](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339#section-5.6). Note: The regular expression provides static schematic guidance but does not reject all invalid dates.

geo-coordinates.description: The geographic latitude and longitude coordinates.
geo-coordinates.title: Geographic Coordinates

href.description: The complete target URL, or link, to use in combination with the method to make the related call, as defined by [RFC 6570 - URI Template](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6570), with the addition of the `$`, `(`, and `)` characters for pre-processing. The `href` is the key HATEOAS component that links a completed call with a subsequent call.

method.description: The method to use to request the link target. For example, for HTTP, this might be `GET` or `DELETE`.

rel.description: The [link relation type](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5988#section-4), which is an identifier for a link that unambiguously describes the semantics of the link. For values, see [Link Relationship Types](https://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/link-relations.xhtml).

submissionMediaType.description: The media type with which to submit data with the request.

submissionSchema.description: The schema that describes the request data.

targetMediaType.description: The [RFC 2046-defined media type](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2046.txt) that describes the link target.

targetSchema.description: The schema that describes the link target.

metafield.description: Metafields enable the consumer to attach additional information to a resource, such as an Order or Line Item

key.description: The unique identifier for the metafield in its namespace

type.description: The type of data that the metafield stores in the `value` field

value.description: The data to store in the metafield. The data is always stored as a string, regardless of the metafield's type

metafield.title: Metafield

patch.description: The JSON patch object to apply partial updates to resources.

from.description: The JSON pointer to the target document location from which to move the value. Required for the `move` operation.

path.description: The JSON pointer to the target document location at which to complete the operation.

value.description: The value to apply. The `remove` operation does not require a value.

patch.title: Patch

percentage.description: A percentage value as a signed decimal number. For example, it defines a 12.34% interest rate as `12.34`.

simple-money.description: The currency and amount for a financial transaction, such as a balance or payment due. Use for value representations with default transactable-value precision.

value.description: The value, which might represent intergrals for currencies like `JPY` that are not typically fractional; or, with an implied decimal fraction for currencies like `TND` that are subdivided into thousandths. For the implied number of decimal places for a currency code, see [ISO-4217 Currency Codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217).
